kinds.name: Kafka
kinds.summary: Reads a stream of records from Kafka topics, or a range of them.

settings.name: brokers
settings.what: The brokers a worker first connects to, `host:port`, separated by commas.

settings.name: topics
settings.what: The topics to read. A matching topic that another source already reads in the same group is left to that source.

settings.name: groupId
settings.what: The consumer group. Readers in one group share the work and resume from the group's saved positions. Set one only when this source needs positions of its own. The leader refuses two sources that read one topic in one consumer group on the same brokers.

settings.name: start
settings.what: Where this source reads from. Changing it will move offsets to the new position.

values.what: Reads from the oldest record each partition holds.

values.what: Stops at the first record at or after `millis`, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

settings.name: identity
settings.what: The [connection identity](/docs/secrets#identities) it connects under, for a private CA or a client certificate. Without one, no certificate is offered and the public roots, Mozilla's and the host's, are trusted.

settings.name: fetchBytes
settings.what: How much fetched input may wait in memory before it is processed. 4 MiB to 512 MiB.

settings.name: encoding
settings.what: How a record's bytes become `_raw`'s text: `auto`, `none`, or a WHATWG encoding label other than the replacement ones, such as `utf-8`, `utf-16le` or `shift_jis`.

values.what: Detects each record's encoding.
Decodes every record as UTF-8, as any other label decodes as its own encoding. Bytes that do not decode become U+FFFD.
Decodes nothing: the record has no `_raw`, and its payload is `__source.bytes` alone. A pipeline reads it as text with `decode(__source.bytes, encoding)`.

kinds.name: HTTP API
kinds.summary: Asks one address with a GET, or a POST of a fixed JSON body, every poll interval, and reads its answer as one record, a record per line, or a record per element of a JSON array. With `sinceParam` it asks only for what is new; without it, every poll reads everything again. One worker reads it. A record's `__source.url` is the address of the page it was read from. For an API that needs more than one request and its pages, use the source made for it.

settings.name: url
settings.what: The whole address it asks, `http://` or `https://`, with any fixed query parameters. It sends a credential only over `https://`, or to this host.

settings.name: method
settings.what: How it asks.

values.what: Asks with a GET.
POSTs `body` on every request, for an API that is asked by what it is sent.

settings.name: body
settings.what: The JSON every POST carries, sent as `application/json` unless `headers` names a `Content-Type`. Only with `method` `POST`.

settings.name: headers
settings.what: Headers it sends on every request, each name to its value. Smeltr sets `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding` and `Host` itself.

settings.name: credentials
settings.what: Headers whose values are secret, each name to the [credential](/docs/secrets) holding its whole value, such as `Bearer <token>`.

settings.name: clientId
settings.what: The OAuth client it signs in as, with `clientSecret` or `privateKey`.

settings.name: clientSecret
settings.what: The [credential](/docs/secrets) holding the OAuth client's secret. Only with `clientId`.

settings.name: privateKey
settings.what: The [credential](/docs/secrets) holding the client's RSA private key, PEM PKCS#8. Replaces `clientSecret`.

settings.name: keyId
settings.what: The `kid` naming `privateKey`, for a client with several keys.

settings.name: tokenUrl
settings.what: Where the client's token is obtained. Replaces `issuer`.

settings.name: issuer
settings.what: The OpenID issuer, exactly as the provider writes it. Replaces `tokenUrl`.

settings.name: scope
settings.what: The scope the client's token is asked for. Only with `clientId`.

settings.name: identity
settings.what: The [connection identity](/docs/secrets#identities) it connects under, for a private CA or a client certificate. Only on an `https://` URL.

settings.name: records
settings.what: Where an answer's records are.

values.what: Gives the whole answer as one record.
Gives one record per line.
Gives one record per element of the JSON array at `recordsAt`.

settings.name: recordsAt
settings.what: The [JSON pointer](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6901) to the array `array` reads, such as `/data` or `/result/items`. An answer with nothing there, or `null`, holds no records. Only with `records` `array`.

settings.name: followLinks
settings.what: Follows each answer's `Link: rel="next"` to the next page, within the same poll. A link to another host is refused, since the credentials go with every request.

settings.name: sinceParam
settings.what: The query parameter that asks for what happened since a time. Each poll sends it the start of the last poll whose records every destination took, in RFC 3339 UTC, such as `2026-10-10T13:00:00.000Z`.

settings.name: sinceOverlapSecs
settings.what: Seconds before the last poll's start that `sinceParam` asks from, for an API that records events late. What falls in the overlap is read twice. Only with `sinceParam`.

settings.name: start
settings.what: What its first poll asks for.

values.what: Asks without `sinceParam`, for everything the API gives.
Asks from the first poll's start. Needs `sinceParam`.

settings.name: pollIntervalSecs
settings.what: Seconds from the start of one poll to the start of the next. At least 1.

kinds.name: Okta System Log

One worker reads it. A record is one event, and its `__source.url` is the address of the page it was read from.

settings.name: org
settings.what: The org's address, with no path. It sends the token only over `https://`, or to this host.

settings.name: token
settings.what: The [credential](/docs/secrets) holding an Okta API token that can read the System Log. It is sent as `Authorization: SSWS <token>`. Give a token, or `clientId` and `privateKey`, never both.

settings.name: clientId
settings.what: The client id of a service app granted the `okta.logs.read` scope and the Read-only Administrator role. The source signs in as the app with a signed key assertion and reads with a token bound to the source's own key by DPoP when Okta binds it. Set both `clientId` and `privateKey`, or neither.

settings.name: privateKey
settings.what: The [credential](/docs/secrets) holding the service app's private key, an RSA key as PEM PKCS#8 (`BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`), whose public half the app holds.

settings.name: keyId
settings.what: The `kid` naming `privateKey`, for a service app with several keys.

settings.name: identity
settings.what: The [connection identity](/docs/secrets#identities) it connects under, for a proxy's private CA.

settings.name: start
settings.what: What its first poll asks for.

values.what: Asks from what Okta lists with no start: its last seven days.
Asks from the first poll's start.

settings.name: pollIntervalSecs
settings.what: Seconds from the start of one poll to the start of the next. At least 1. A rate limit is waited out until the reset Okta names.

kinds.name: PostgreSQL
kinds.summary: Runs a query you write against a PostgreSQL database every poll, and reads each row of its result as one record, a field per column. Smeltr runs the query inside a statement of its own, which adds the position test, the order and the batch limit. How it knows a row is due is its `mode`, cheapest first. One worker reads it, and the leader keeps how far it has read, so a restart or a move to another worker reads from there: a duplicate, never a loss. A record's `__source.database` is the database it was read from, as `host:port/database`.

settings.name: host
settings.what: The database server's host name or address.

settings.name: port
settings.what: The server's port.

settings.name: database
settings.what: The database the query runs in.

settings.name: user
settings.what: The user it connects as. Give it read access and nothing more: the query runs in a read-only transaction, but only the user's own grants keep a source from writing.

settings.name: password
settings.absent: none, for a server that asks for no password
settings.what: The [credential](/docs/secrets) holding the user's password.

settings.name: tls
settings.what: Whether the connection is encrypted.

values.what: Encrypts, and verifies the server's certificate and its name.
Sends everything in the clear, the password too.

settings.name: identity
settings.what: The [connection identity](/docs/secrets#identities) it connects under: the authorities it trusts for the server's certificate, and a certificate to present. Only with `tls` `require`.

settings.name: query
examples: SELECT event_id, occurred_at, user_name FROM auth.events
SELECT event_id, occurred_at, user_name FROM auth.events WHERE (:last.occurred_at IS NULL OR occurred_at >= :last.occurred_at)
settings.what: A `SELECT` or a `WITH`, with no `ORDER BY` or `LIMIT` of its own: the statement around it orders by the position and sets the batch. `:last.<field>` is the value that field held in the last row sent, `NULL` before the first, for a filter the statement's own cannot reach, such as one inside a `GROUP BY`. The statement still reads past the last row sent, so the filter keeps the last value (`>=`) and rows sharing it are not lost.

settings.name: mode
settings.what: How it knows a row is due. `position` is the field rows are read in the order of, then the fields that tell apart rows with the same value in it. A position that starts with a datetime waits `settleSecs` (default 30) behind the database's clock for late commits. A source with no progress begins where `start` says: `"now"` (default) at the largest position the query returns on its first poll, `"beginning"` at every row, or `"from"` at `startFrom`, an integer or an ISO 8601 time with its offset.

values.what: Each row once, by a field that only grows as rows are added: an id, or the time it was inserted. Reads only the new rows.
Each row when it is added and again each time it changes, by a datetime every insert and update sets. A deleted row is not seen.
Each row when its `key` is new or its values changed, by reading the whole result every poll. Up to a million rows; the leader keeps an entry for each.
The whole result every poll. Nothing is remembered.

settings.name: fields
settings.what: Each field of the record: the result column of the same `name`, and its `type` as a pipeline spells one, such as `i64`, `datetime`, `str`, `bytes` or `array<str>`. A column the fields do not name is not read.

settings.name: pollIntervalSecs
settings.what: Seconds from the start of one poll to the start of the next. At least 1. A poll that reads a full batch reads the next at once.

settings.name: batch
settings.what: The most rows one poll reads by a position. With no field after the first in `position`, a full poll leaves its last rows sharing one value to the next, which reads up to twice `batch` when they fill a poll; past that, the rest of the rows sharing that value are skipped with a warning. In `everyPoll`, a result with more fails the poll. Between 1 and 100000.

kinds.name: HTTP receiver
kinds.summary: Takes what senders POST to a path on its port: a webhook, a log shipper, a script. Every worker of the group listens, and a sender, or a balancer in front of the workers, picks one. A request is answered `200` only once every destination has its records, so a sender that retries an unanswered request loses nothing. A full or blocked receiver answers `503` with `Retry-After` at once. `GET /health` answers `200` while it takes requests, for a balancer's health check. A record's `__source.remote` is the sender's address.

settings.name: port
settings.what: The port it listens on. Every worker of the group binds it, so no two receivers share one.

settings.name: path
settings.what: The path senders POST to. It starts with `/` and holds no `?`, `#`, `:`, `*` or space. Not `/health`, where it answers health checks.

settings.name: tokens
settings.what: Each token's name to the [credential](/docs/secrets) holding it. A sender presents one as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, and any other request is refused `401`. A receiver with no token needs an `identity` with authorities.

settings.name: identity
settings.what: The [connection identity](/docs/secrets#identities) it serves TLS under: its certificate and key. With authorities, a sender must present a certificate that chains to one of them.

settings.name: records
settings.what: Where a request body's records are.

values.what: Gives the whole body as one record.
Gives one record per line.
Gives one record per element of the JSON array at `recordsAt`.

settings.name: recordsAt
settings.what: The [JSON pointer](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6901) to the array `array` reads. A body with no array there is refused `400`. Only with `records` `array`.

settings.name: maxRequestBytes
settings.what: The largest request body it reads, between 1024 and 67108864. A larger one is refused `413`. A body sent as gzip is held to it as it inflates.

kinds.name: HEC receiver
kinds.summary: Takes what Splunk HTTP Event Collector clients send to its port, at the paths Splunk serves: OpenTelemetry Collectors, Fluent Bit, logging libraries and other HEC clients. A Splunk forwarder's `httpout` posts S2S to `/services/collector/s2s`, which it takes; a forwarder sending with `tcpout` needs an S2S receiver. Every worker of the group listens, and a sender, or a balancer in front of the workers, picks one. A request is answered `Success` only once every destination has its events. A sender whose token has `acknowledgement` names a channel and is given an `ackId` at once instead; `/services/collector/ack` reports it `true` once every destination has its events. Only the worker that gave an ID can report it, so a balancer must keep a channel on one worker. A full or blocked receiver answers code `9` with `Retry-After` at once. Each event is a record, filed under the `__source` fields its envelope names.

settings.name: port
settings.what: The port it listens on. Every worker of the group binds it, so no two receivers share one.

settings.name: tokens
settings.what: Each token's name to its `token`, the [credential](/docs/secrets) holding it, and `acknowledgement`. A sender presents a token as `Authorization: Splunk <token>`, and any other request is refused with code `2`, `3` or `4`. With `acknowledgement` true, as Splunk's `useACK`, its senders name a channel and are answered at once with an `ackId`, and one that names none is refused code `10`; without it, a request is held until delivered and `/services/collector/ack` answers code `14`. A receiver with no token needs an `identity` with authorities, and holds every request.

settings.name: identity
settings.what: The [connection identity](/docs/secrets#identities) it serves TLS under: its certificate and key. With authorities, a sender must present a certificate that chains to one of them.

settings.name: sourcetypes
settings.absent: a record per line for every sourcetype
settings.what: Maps each sourcetype to a lineBreaker, which splits text into multiple events. Its first capture group is the break and is dropped: the bytes before it end an event, line ends and all, and the bytes after it start the next. It needs a capture group and must not match the empty string. A raw request of a sourcetype not named, or named with no `lineBreaker` or with `([\r\n]+)`, is a record per line. The event endpoint's envelopes are not broken.

settings.name: maxRequestBytes
settings.what: The largest request body it reads, between 1024 and 67108864. A larger one is refused `413`. A body sent as gzip is held to it as it inflates.

kinds.name: S2S receiver
kinds.summary: Takes what Splunk forwarders send over Splunk-to-Splunk (S2S). Every worker of the group listens. A forwarder with `useACK` is acknowledged each event once every destination has its records, so delivery is at least once; without it, delivery is best-effort. A full or blocked receiver stops reading until its destinations take records again. Each event is a record, filed under the `__source` fields the forwarder names.

settings.name: port
settings.what: The port it listens on. Every worker of the group binds it, so no two receivers share one.

settings.name: tokens
settings.what: Each token's name to the [credential](/docs/secrets) holding it. A forwarder presents one as its outputs.conf `token`, and one that presents none or another is cut off. A receiver with no token needs an `identity` with authorities.

settings.name: identity
settings.what: The [connection identity](/docs/secrets#identities) it serves TLS under: its certificate and key. With authorities, a forwarder must present a certificate that chains to one of them.

settings.name: sourcetypes
settings.absent: an event per line for every sourcetype

settings.name: maxRequestBytes
settings.what: The largest frame it reads, and the most one record holds, between 1024 and 67108864.

kinds.name: OTLP receiver
kinds.summary: Takes what OpenTelemetry exporters send over OTLP to its port: OpenTelemetry SDKs, Collectors and other OTLP clients. It takes one `signal`, logs, metrics or traces, over HTTP as protobuf or JSON and over gRPC. Receivers of different signals may share one port; an export of a signal no receiver there takes is refused `404`, or `UNIMPLEMENTED` over gRPC. Every worker of the group listens, and a sender, or a balancer in front of the workers, picks one. An export is answered `200` only once every destination has its records, so an exporter that retries an unanswered export loses nothing. A full or blocked receiver answers `503` with `Retry-After` at once, which an exporter may retry; a body that does not read is refused `400`, which it may drop. Each log record, metric data point or span is a record of typed fields, as OTLP types them. Its resource and scope are `__source` fields.

settings.name: port
settings.what: The port it listens on. Every worker of the group binds it, so no two receivers share one, but OTLP receivers of different signals may, with the same `identity` certificate.

settings.name: signal
settings.what: The signal it takes, each a record of its own fields.

values.what: Gives one record per log record, from `/v1/logs` and the logs gRPC service.
Gives one record per metric data point, from `/v1/metrics` and the metrics gRPC service.
Gives one record per span, from `/v1/traces` and the trace gRPC service.

settings.name: tokens
settings.what: Each token's name to the [credential](/docs/secrets) holding it. An exporter presents one as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, and any other request is refused `401`. A receiver with no token needs an `identity` with authorities.

settings.name: identity
settings.what: The [connection identity](/docs/secrets#identities) it serves TLS under: its certificate and key. With authorities, a sender must present a certificate that chains to one of them.

settings.name: maxRequestBytes
settings.what: The largest request body it reads, between 1024 and 67108864. A larger one is refused `413`. A body sent as gzip is held to it as it inflates.

kinds.name: Syslog receiver
kinds.summary: Takes what syslog senders send to its port, over TCP or UDP: rsyslog, syslog-ng, network devices and appliances. Messages are RFC 5424 or RFC 3164. Over TCP each is framed by its octet count or ended by a newline (RFC 6587). With `lineBreaker` set, it ends where the pattern breaks instead of at a newline. Under an `identity`, TCP is served over TLS (RFC 5425). Over UDP each datagram is one message (RFC 5426), served without TLS. Every worker of the group listens, and a sender, or a balancer in front of the workers, picks one. Syslog carries no token, so a receiver admits senders by the networks in `allowFrom`, by a certificate that chains to its identity's authorities, or both; over UDP by `allowFrom` alone. Syslog has no acknowledgement: delivery is best-effort. What a connection carries when it is cut, and what a worker holds when it stops, is lost. A full or blocked receiver stops reading TCP, so the sender's TCP window fills and the sender buffers or drops by its own rules. It drops a datagram that arrives while it is full or blocked, and counts it in `smeltr_source_dropped_total`. Each message is a record whose `_raw` is the message as sent, its PRI header included; a pipeline parses the header.

settings.name: port
settings.what: The port it listens on. Every worker of the group binds it, so no two receivers of one `transport` share one; a TCP and a UDP receiver may.

settings.name: transport
settings.what: What senders send over.

values.what: Takes connections, under TLS when it names an `identity`. A full receiver stops reading, which slows the sender.

Takes datagrams, one message each, for senders that send only UDP. No TLS, and nothing slows a sender: a datagram that arrives while the receiver is full or blocked is dropped and counted in `smeltr_source_dropped_total`. It needs `allowFrom`.

settings.name: allowFrom
settings.what: The networks a sender may connect from: CIDR blocks such as `10.0.0.0/8`, or single addresses. A connection from anywhere else is closed before any of it is read, and a datagram from anywhere else is dropped. Without it, a TCP receiver needs an `identity` with authorities, and admits every sender whose certificate chains to one of them. A UDP receiver needs it. A datagram's source address is whatever its sender writes, so over UDP it admits whoever can reach the port and claim an address in these networks.

settings.what: The access tier each blob is stored in: `Hot`, `Cool`, `Cold` or `Archive`.

settings.name: identity
settings.what: The [connection identity](/docs/secrets#identities) it connects under, for a private CA or a client certificate.

kinds.name: SFTP
kinds.summary: Writes each batch into a directory on an SFTP server as one file per prefix. Each file is written under a hidden temporary name beside its own and renamed into place, so a reader never sees part of one.

settings.name: host
settings.what: The server's host name or address.

settings.name: port
settings.what: The server's SSH port.

settings.name: username
settings.what: The user it signs in as, who needs write access to `directory`.

settings.name: password
settings.what: The [credential](/docs/secrets) holding the user's password. Set exactly one of `password` and `privateKey`.

settings.name: privateKey
settings.what: The [credential](/docs/secrets) holding the user's private key: an unencrypted RSA, ed25519 or ECDSA key in OpenSSH's format.

settings.name: hostKey
settings.what: The server's public key as OpenSSH writes it, `ssh-ed25519 AAAA…`, without a host name: it connects to that server and no other. Copy it from the server's `/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub`, or from `ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 sftp.example.com`, dropping the host name it starts with; keyscan trusts the network it asks over, so check its answer against the server's file.

settings.name: directory
settings.what: The directory it writes into: absolute, or under the user's home directory. Empty is the home directory. It must exist, as a bucket must; the folders a prefix names under it are made as needed.

kinds.name: Apache Iceberg
kinds.summary: Writes Parquet files to an Iceberg table in S3 and commits them through its REST catalog.

settings.name: catalog
settings.what: The REST catalog's base address, before `/v1`.

settings.name: warehouse
settings.what: The warehouse the catalog serves the table from.

settings.name: namespace
settings.what: The table's namespace, its levels joined by dots.

settings.name: table
settings.what: The table it writes. A missing table is created from the route's record.

settings.name: partitionBy
settings.what: How a table it creates is partitioned: a column, or `year`, `month`, `day` or `hour` of one, or `bucket(n, column)` or `truncate(width, column)`. A table that exists keeps its own.

settings.name: token
settings.what: The [credential](/docs/secrets) holding a bearer token for the catalog. Not with `clientId`.

settings.name: clientId
settings.what: The OAuth client it signs in to the catalog as, with `clientSecret`.

settings.name: clientSecret
settings.what: The [credential](/docs/secrets) holding the OAuth client's secret. Only with `clientId`.

settings.name: tokenUrl
settings.what: Where the client's token is obtained. Only with `clientId`.

settings.name: scope
settings.what: The scope the client's token is asked for. Use the scope your catalog takes. Only with `clientId`.

settings.name: signingName
settings.what: Signs every catalog call with AWS Signature Version 4 for this service, with the AWS credentials storage names, else the host's, in the region the catalog's AWS address names, else its `region`: `glue` for Glue's Iceberg endpoint, `s3tables` for S3 Tables. Needs `region` when the address names none. Not with `token` or `clientId`.

settings.name: region
settings.absent: the region the catalog gives the table, else the one the catalog's AWS address names, else the host's, else `us-east-1`
settings.what: The bucket's region.

settings.name: endpoint
settings.absent: the one the catalog gives the table, else the host's, else AWS
settings.what: An S3-compatible service's address. Without an access key, the worker host's AWS settings, such as `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, come after the catalog's.

settings.name: accessKeyId
settings.absent: what the catalog vends, else the host's credentials
settings.what: The [credential](/docs/secrets) holding the access key's id. Set both `accessKeyId` and `secretAccessKey`, or neither.

settings.name: secretAccessKey
settings.absent: what the catalog vends, else the host's credentials
settings.what: The [credential](/docs/secrets) holding the access key's secret.

settings.name: roleArn
settings.what: A role to assume, for a bucket in another account.

settings.name: externalId
settings.what: The external id the role requires. Only with `roleArn`.

settings.name: authEndpoint
settings.what: Where the role in `roleArn` is assumed. Only with `roleArn`.

settings.name: identity
settings.what: The [connection identity](/docs/secrets#identities) it connects to the catalog and the store under, for a private CA or a client certificate.

settings.name: compression
settings.what: How each Parquet file compresses its columns.

values.what: Writes columns uncompressed.
Compresses columns with gzip.
Compresses columns with Snappy.
Compresses columns with LZ4.
Compresses columns with Zstandard.

settings.name: inFlight
settings.what: How many parts of one file upload at once. 1 to 64.

settings.name: maxObjectBytes
settings.what: The largest data file it writes, compressed. 64 KiB to 64 GiB.

settings.name: bufferBytes
settings.what: Memory it may use on each worker for records not yet committed. Files are committed early when it fills. 4 MiB to 32 TiB.

settings.name: stallAfterSecs
settings.what: Seconds one call to the store or the catalog, or one commit, may take before it counts as stalled. 1 to 120.

settings.name: fileIntervalSecs
settings.what: The longest records wait, in seconds, before they are committed to the table. Each commit is a snapshot the table keeps until it is expired; records are acknowledged only once committed, so a source is held open up to this long. 5 to 240.
